The US FDA has approved Cirium's radioligand therapy Bexlutry (lutetium Lu 177 dotatate) for receptor-positive gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, the first such generic treatment approved for Novartis'
Approval was based on bridging data showing a similar biological and chemical profile to Lutathera.
Like Lutathera, Bexlutry works by delivering targeted radiation to tumors by binding to somatostatin receptors frequently expressed on the tumors.
Novartis reported $436M in Lutathera sales in the first half of 2026.
The approval follows Cirium's August announcement it would acquire Lantheus Holdings

title: Novartis' Lutathera now facing generic competition from Cirium's Bexlutry
